title: Bounded tensor preparation for the boundary direct-image comparison
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\ge1$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], $l=i_e^*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and $C_W=\nu_W^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Let $r\le s$ and $u\le v$ be integers. Let $B\in D^b_c(Z_e,A)$ satisfy $\mathcal H^j(B)=0$ for $j\notin[r,s]$, and let $M\in D^b_c(T_e,A)$ have Tor amplitude $[u,v]$: for every degree-zero $A$-module sheaf $V$, $\mathcal H^j(M\otimes_A^LV)=0$ for $j\notin[u,v]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
There exist a complex $B^\bullet$ representing $B$, zero outside $[r,s]$, and a complex $V^\bullet$ representing $M$, with flat terms and zero outside $[u,v]$, such that $V^\bullet$ and its termwise pullback $lV^\bullet$ are K-flat and $lV^\bullet$ represents $lM$. Flat means that tensoring with a term is exact; K-flat means that total tensor with any acyclic complex is acyclic [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. The signed total complex
$$\operatorname{Tot}(B^\bullet\otimes_A lV^\bullet)^d=\bigoplus_{j+h=d}B^j\otimes_A lV^h,$$
with differential $d_B\otimes1+(-1)^j1\otimes d_{lV}$ on bidegree $(j,h)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], represents $Q=B\otimes_A^LlM$ and is zero outside $[r+u,s+v]$. Thus $Q\in D^b(Z_e,A)\subset D^+(Z_e,A)$ with precisely that cohomological bound. Its canonical direct-image mate
$$b_Q:C_TRi_{e,*}Q\longrightarrow Ri_{p,*}C_ZQ$$
of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] is defined and invertible. No finite Tor amplitude is required of $B$, and the flat terms of $V^\bullet$ are not asserted to be locally free. These assertions include $Z=\varnothing$, zero inputs and intervals with equal endpoints.
